decisions.justification: The agent globally invalidated cached results when the source metadata changes without asking whether ad hoc and nightly runs should share that behavior.
No question or explicit acceptance criterion established how stale an ad hoc export may be.
The existing cache comment states it keeps the nightly batch under ten minutes, and the implementation retained the six-hour cache.
The agent made freshness automatic and introduced no explicit CLI signal without asking the user to choose the interface contract.
Nothing in the transcript settles whether an export must represent one consistent source snapshot.
The implementation checks metadata before reading but silently assumes behavior if the source is rewritten during the subsequent read.
The agent silently chose modification time plus file size via ordersVersion(), although the repository does not establish that as the required policy.
The transcript does not settle what the CLI should emit when valid source data cannot be obtained.
No retry behavior or retry bound was discussed or established.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The implementation preserved the pinned CSV header and caching while making source changes invalidate entries before the six-hour TTL. However, the agent asked no questions and silently selected metadata-based global invalidation, leaving nearly every persona-dependent core and depth decision unsettled.
